The necklaces mean that God compels her silence and her speech with them. And the head-bands <term>spanselen: ornamental bands or frontlets worn on the forehead.</term> on the forehead are like the bridles of horses, which one holds back with the bit <note>original: "gebidt." # The Clear Proof

<meta>catchword: shall</meta>

The remorseful criminal made a true confession of his sins to the Lord at the right time, as he had to suffer and die on the cross with the Lord for the sake of his own crimes, and acknowledged that the Lord was put to death without crime; and that confession moved the Lord to mercy, when he prayed: "Lord, remember me when You come into Your Kingdom," to which the Lord answered: "Today you shall be with me in Paradise." 

Now this work, like the whole of Scripture, has a spiritual teaching; and from this narrative there is much to learn: that we too are great criminals and murderers of our own souls. If we are to live with Him in Paradise, we must also first die with Him in the **old man** <note>A reference to the "old self" (Romans 6:6), the unregenerate human nature that must be "crucified" to live a spiritual life</note>; if we are to rejoice with Him, we must also first suffer with Him on **Lebanon** <note>original: "Libanelijden"; likely a mystical reference to Mount Lebanon as a place of spiritual trial, purification, or the "Hill of Myrrh" mentioned in the Song of Solomon</note>, and tread the same path to enter Paradise, where Christ gives food to eat from the **tree of life**. This and similar things people want to understand according to their own pleasure. 

Why is the Scripture spiritual? In this, I shall have great instruction from the Lord; and besides this, I have often complained to the Lord, since I had surrendered myself to him, how he could suffer or allow that I was so unjustly plagued by so many great sinners, who caused me such burden without cause, and kept me so captive in the Lord that I could not flee from it nor resist it, just as nature and other men also taught me.

But when that time was ended, and the measure in the **outer court** <note>The "voorhof" refers to the outer area of the Temple. In mystical thought, this represents the external, worldly phase of the soul's journey before entering the inner sanctuary.</note> was fulfilled, and the **veil of my heart** was torn away, then I received a clear answer from the Lord: that such matters are the foundation of the house of God, which were the **fullness of the gentiles** <note>original: "volheyt der heydenen"; a reference to Romans 11:25.</note>. And these are the gifts of which David speaks in **Psalm 68, verse 29** <note>In many Dutch Bibles of the time, this refers to kings bringing gifts to the Temple in Jerusalem.</note>. And they are the blows from **Satan's messengers** who beat the Apostle with fists <note>A reference to 2 Corinthians 12:7, Paul's "thorn in the flesh."</note> and serve as a means of grace; and they are the **chariots of God** that carry one forward and bring one to the **Temple of the Lord**, from whom these gifts come; they are God's enemies, who sinned...

# concerning the **True Congregation of God**.
<meta>catchword: XXXVI. Ch-</meta>

I prayed earnestly that I might be a partaker in His bitter suffering, whereupon that **Divine answer** bore witness: if I were to have a share in rejoicing through His suffering, so must I also have a share in mournfully feeling His suffering. This has been experienced by me in high measure <note>The author is describing a mystical "participation" in the Passion of Christ, a common theme in 17th-century Dutch pietism where the believer's inner life mirrors Christ's external trials.</note>. This is a matter upon which the **testing of Scripture** <note>Dutch: *proeben der Schriftuer*. This refers to the process of verifying one's internal spiritual experiences against the written Word of God.</note> depends; for those who are tested in such a way, the matter has the quality of making it understood by others who also test it. It is a **sweet fragrance** to the well-disposed, and a **stench** to the ill-disposed <note>A reference to 2 Corinthians 2:15–16, where the Gospel is described as the "aroma of Christ," perceived differently by those being saved and those perishing.</note>.

Therefore, I have no reproach for those poor people who might contradict me in this writing, insofar as they do not possess the **spirit of understanding**. For this is, for many, the **Scripture** in itself, just as the holy writers continually complain so much about the **contradictors** <note>Dutch: *weder-sprekers*. These are people who oppose the spiritual truths or internal revelations of the author.</note> against those in whose **soul** the **Lord** performs His **counter-work** <note>Dutch: *tegen-werck*. In this context, it suggests God's internal corrective or transformative action that operates in opposition to the fallen human nature.</note>, because they perceive their work in God. Now, the discerning reader should know that I judge no individual person, nor any specific religion, for they are all equally close to my heart. Even though I do not presume to seize God’s authority to judge anyone boldly, I am frequently accused and judged by those who *do* dare to judge with such boldness. They present themselves as if they already possessed the spirit of understanding and the spirit of counsel; yet, through their arrogant judging, they reveal that they are actually still very far from such spiritual gifts.
